questions.explanation: var infers the initializer's static type; Object explicitly declares the broader type.

questions.question: What does pattern matching for instanceof allow?
options: Casting without checks.
Declaring variables without types.
A type test and conditional pattern-variable declaration in one expression.
Skipping null checks.
questions.explanation: Pattern-variable scope depends on flow analysis and whether the pattern is definitely matched.

questions.question: In which Java version did pattern matching for switch become permanent?
options: Java 17
Java 14
Java 21
Java 11
questions.explanation: Pattern matching for switch was finalized in Java 21.

questions.question: How does Objects.equals(a,b) differ from a == b when references may be null?
options: Objects.equals safely handles null and delegates to equals(); == tests identity.
Objects.equals throws NullPointerException on null; == does not.
They are identical.
Objects.equals compares identity; == delegates to equals().
questions.explanation: Objects.equals(null, null) returns true and one-null comparisons return false.

questions.question: Can Java declare a normal named method directly inside another method?
options: Yes; a method may declare nested methods.
Yes, but only static methods.
No; use a lambda or local class instead.
Yes, but only private methods.
questions.explanation: Local classes, anonymous classes, and lambdas are possible, but ordinary nested method declarations are not.

questions.question: If class A has a static initializer printing A, an instance initializer printing B, and a constructor printing C, what does new A(); new A(); print?
options: ABCBC
ABC
ABCABC
BCBC
questions.explanation: The static initializer runs once; instance initialization and the constructor run for each object.

questions.question: If Parent's constructor prints P and Child's constructor prints C, what does new Child() print when Child extends Parent?
options: PC
CP
P only
C only
questions.explanation: The superclass constructor runs before the subclass constructor body.

questions.question: Why does class B extends A fail to compile if A declares only a private no-argument constructor and B declares no constructor?
options: Classes with a private constructor must be declared final.
B must be declared abstract.
B's implicit constructor cannot access A().
A private constructor makes A an interface.
questions.explanation: The subclass needs an accessible superclass constructor.

questions.question: If A overloads f(Number) and f(Integer), Number n = 10; new A().f(n) calls which overload?
options: f(Integer)
Compilation error (ambiguous)
A ClassCastException at runtime
f(Number)
questions.explanation: Overload resolution uses the compile-time type Number.

questions.question: What is the risk of removing from an ArrayList directly inside an enhanced for loop?
options: The loop skips elements silently without errors.
Always an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
ConcurrentModificationException may occur.
An IllegalStateException is always thrown.
questions.explanation: The collection is structurally modified outside the iterator; use Iterator.remove() or an appropriate collection operation.

questions.question: Is a counter with volatile int count and count++ thread-safe?
options: No; count++ is still a non-atomic read-modify-write.
Yes; volatile makes increment atomic.
Yes, but only on a single-core CPU.
Yes, if the field is private.
questions.explanation: The increment is a compound read-modify-write operation; use atomic operations or synchronization.

questions.question: What does map.getOrDefault("x", 0) return after a HashMap maps "x" to 1?
options: null
Throws NoSuchElementException
questions.explanation: getOrDefault returns the mapped value when the key is mapped.

questions.question: If a RuntimeException with message A is caught and finally prints B, what is printed?
options: A only
B, then A
A, then B
B only
questions.explanation: The catch prints the message and finally runs afterward.

questions.question: Does a class compile if it implements two interfaces that define conflicting default methods with the same signature but does not override the method?
options: Yes; the compiler picks the first one.
Yes; the compiler picks the one from the alphabetically earlier interface.
Yes; both are called.
No; the class must override the method to resolve the conflict.
questions.explanation: The class must resolve the conflict, typically by overriding the method.

questions.question: Why distinguish a Java language guarantee from a common JVM implementation detail?
options: Because everything the JVM does is specified.
Because implementation details are always the same across JVMs.
Only specified behavior is guaranteed across conforming implementations; implementation details may vary.
Because language rules do not apply on the JVM.
questions.explanation: Interview answers should separate specification guarantees from observed behavior on one JVM.
